objective: Create app/audit.py implementing the C1 hash-chain core: GENESIS marker, entry hashing (sha256 over canonical JSON of {id, prev_entry_hash}), and verify(items) that recomputes every entry_hash, checks every link over an oldest-first list of stored item dicts, and returns {status: 'ok'|'broken'|'unanchored_head', first_broken_link, head: {event_id, anchored}} without raising on broken chains; observable outcome: tests/test_audit_core.py passes, proving an unmodified chain verifies anchored at GENESIS, a rewritten middle entry is detected, and a mid-removed entry is detected.

concepts: sha256 over canonical JSON (json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')).encode('utf-8'))
hash-chain link invariant: item[i].prev_entry_hash == item[i-1].entry_hash; item[0].prev_entry_hash == GENESIS
windowed verifiability semantics: anchored at GENESIS until the first overwrite drops the genesis item, then 'unanchored_head' (links among surviving items are still checked)

inputs: contract C1 (full spec inlined in frozen_contracts — the only spec source; do not open stage-contract.json)
acceptance A1 semantics (windowed verification result shape)

frozen_contracts.spec: Audit entry data stored inside each event item in the RingBuffer: the stored item is {id: 'e<n>', <event payload fields>, prev_entry_hash: str, entry_hash: str} where prev_entry_hash = entry_hash of the previously appended item (or GENESIS = sha256(b'genesis').hexdigest() for the first item ever appended) and entry_hash = sha256(canonical_json({id, prev_entry_hash})).hexdigest() with canonical_json = json.dumps(obj, sort_keys=True, separators=(',', ':')). Chain order = RingBuffer storage order (oldest surviving first). The API layer never exposes prev_entry_hash/entry_hash outside the C3 query.

non_goals: No changes to app/events.py, app/storage.py, or tests/test_events.py
No import of EventAPI or RingBuffer — verify() and the hash helpers operate on plain lists/dicts of items
No external anchoring, no second store, no persistence beyond the in-item fields
No hashing performance work (out of scope per contract)
implementation_constraints: Hash exactly per C1: entry_hash = hashlib.sha256(canonical_json({'id': item['id'], 'prev_entry_hash': item['prev_entry_hash']})).hexdigest() where canonical_json uses sort_keys=True and separators=(',', ':'), encoded utf-8
verify(items) must never raise on broken or unanchored chains — it returns the structured dict {status, first_broken_link, head}
head.anchored is True iff items is non-empty and items[0].prev_entry_hash == GENESIS
missing prev_entry_hash/entry_hash keys on an item count as a broken link at that item (no KeyError)
pure stdlib (hashlib, json); Python 3.10+; no third-party dependencies
test style: unittest (matching the repo suite), plain asserts, deterministic, in-memory only

deliverables.what: chain hashing + verify module per C1 (pure functions over item lists)
unit tests: link integrity, rewrite detection, mid-truncation detection

acceptance_tests.description: A 4-item chain built per C1 (first item prev = GENESIS, each next prev = previous entry_hash) verifies: status 'ok', first_broken_link None, head anchored True
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_audit_core.test_chain_verifies_ok -v → 1 test passes, exit code 0

acceptance_tests.description: Rewriting a middle item's payload (keeping its id) makes verify() return status 'broken' with first_broken_link identifying that item (hash mismatch)
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_audit_core.test_rewrite_detected -v → 1 test passes, exit code 0

acceptance_tests.description: Deleting a middle item (simulating mid-truncation) makes verify() return status 'broken' with first_broken_link at the dangling link (survivor's prev matches no stored entry_hash)
acceptance_tests.evidence: python -m unittest tests.test_audit_core.test_mid_truncation_detected -v → 1 test passes, exit code 0

failure_cases.scenario: verify() called on an empty list
failure_cases.expected_behavior: returns {status: 'ok', first_broken_link: None, head: None} — vacuously valid, no exception
status 'unanchored_head'; links still checked; first_broken_link reports the first link/hash failure if any, else None

failure_cases.scenario: an item lacks prev_entry_hash or entry_hash keys
failure_cases.expected_behavior: verify() returns status 'broken' with first_broken_link set at that item; no KeyError is raised

handoff.notes: T02 imports app.audit: expose exactly the surface C1's spec implies (entry hashing + verify over an oldest-first item list). verify() consumes item dicts with at least id/prev_entry_hash/entry_hash keys in storage order. If T03 later finds a seam defect that requires touching this module, the fix goes through T03's owns_fixes_for route with a deviation recorded in T03's checkpoint.
